```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta}
mod <- readModelDb("Wilson_2020_hematopoiesis_invitro")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
drugPar <- ui$meta$drugEffectParameters
names(drugPar)
```

* Citation: Wilson JL, Lu D, Corr N, Fullerton A, Lu J. An in vitro
  quantitative systems pharmacology approach for deconvolving mechanisms of
  drug-induced, multilineage cytopenias. *PLoS Comput Biol*
  2020;16(7):e1007620. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007620>
  (open access, PMC7402526).
* Supporting information used here: S1 Text (the SimBiology export of every
  flux, ODE, rule, event and parameter value), S3 Text (the mapping between
  the Greek-letter names of the figures and the MATLAB names), S1 Table (the
  vehicle-normalized day-6 cell counts of the drug-treatment experiment) and
  S2 Table (the fitted EmaxT and log(EC50) of every compound). The SimBiology
  project is also deposited at
  <https://github.com/jenwilson521/Multilineage_InvitroHem_Model>.

The model describes hematopoiesis in a 6-day culture of human bone-marrow
CD34+ cells (the multilineage toxicity assay, MLTA). Hematopoietic stem cells
(HSC) renew themselves and feed multipotent progenitors (MPP); MPP branch into
granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GMP), megakaryocytes (MK), early erythroid
cells and lymphoid progenitors; GMP branch into monocyte and granulocyte
progenitors, which mature into monocytes and granulocytes, and granulocytes
feed a proliferating and a quiescent neutrophil pool. Early erythroid cells
mature into late erythroid cells, and lymphoid progenitors into B cells. Each
division makes two daughters that renew with probability rho or
differentiate with probability 1 - rho (Fig 2B). Only the most mature cell of
each lineage dies, at one shared rate `kdeath`.

A drug acts on every cell type through **one** total Emax (EmaxT) and one
log(EC50) per cell type. The part of EmaxT up to 1 inhibits the basal
proliferation rate; the part above 1 is a first-order kill rate in 1/day:

    kpro   = kpro0 * (1 - min(1, EmaxT) * C / (EC50 + C))
    kkill  = max(0, EmaxT - 1) * C / (EC50 + C)

The packaged `ini()` holds the system parameters calibrated to drug-free
kinetics with every drug effect off (`emaxt_* = 0`). The fitted drug-effect
sets are in `ui$meta$drugEffectParameters`, one named vector per compound,
and are passed to `rxSolve(params = )`.

# Population

The system parameters and the 14 initial cell counts were fitted to the mean
of six donor samples of CD34+ cells cultured without drug and counted on days
2 to 6 (days 0 and 9 were dropped; see Results, "The model explains cell
kinetic data in the absence of drug treatment"). The drug-effect parameters
were fitted, one compound at a time, to day-6 counts after exposure to 0.2,
1, 5, 25, 100, 500 and 2500 nM added on day 0, normalized to vehicle-control
wells and pooled over 2-7 donor samples (S1 Table). Because the fits are to
donor means, the model is deterministic: it carries no between-donor
variability and no residual error.

# Source trace

| Element | Value(s) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Flux equations (`r1` ... `r32`, `kill_*`) | 38 fluxes | S1 Text, "Fluxes" |
| ODE stoichiometry (15 cell states + drug) | as printed | S1 Text, "ODEs" |
| Anti-proliferation rule `kpro = kpro0 * (1 - min(1, EmaxT) * C/(EC50 + C))` | 12 cell types | S1 Text rules 5-16; Methods Eq 2 |
| Cell-kill rule `max(0, EmaxT - 1) * C/(EC50 + C)` (1/day) | 13 cell types | S1 Text rules 17-29 and fluxes 25-38; Methods Eq 3 |
| Neutrophil quiescent split `QF_Neutrophil * initNeutrophil` | at t = 0.01 day | S1 Text, "Events" |
| `totalViableCells`, `viability`, `Neutrophil-lin` | sums | S1 Text, "Repeated Assignments" |
| `kpro0_*` (12), `renew_*` (7), `kbranch_*` (4), `kdeath`, `kdiff_lym`, `qf_neut` | 26 values | S1 Text, "Parameters (Model Scoped)" |
| `bl_*` (14 initial counts) | cells/mL | S1 Text, "Species - InVitro" (1 mL compartment) |
| `emaxt_*` = 0, `lec50_*` = 1 (drug-free defaults) | 26 values | S1 Text, "Parameters (Model Scoped)" |
| `drugEffectParameters` (14 named compounds) | 26 values each | S2 Table, sheet "log_EC50_parameters_from_fittin"; Table 1 (rounded) |
| Parameter-name mapping (rho, kappa, beta, delta) | | S3 Text |
| Day-6 normalized observations used below | 8 compounds | S1 Table |

# Drug-free kinetics

## Cross-checks against S1 Text

S1 Text lists the initial `viability` as 0.785724947286575. It is a function
of the fitted initial counts alone, so it checks the 14 `bl_*` values and the
`totalViableCells` sum.

```{r control-sim}
evCtl <- et(amt = 0, cmt = "drug", time = 0) |>
  et(seq(0, 6, by = 0.05))
simCtl <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(ui, evCtl))
v0 <- simCtl$viability[simCtl$time == 0]
v0
stopifnot(abs(v0 - 0.785724947286575) < 1e-9)
```

## Replicates Figure 3 of Wilson 2020

```{r fig3, fig.height = 6}
cellCols <- c(
  HSC = "hsc", MPP = "mpp", GMP = "gmp", "Gran-lin prog" = "gran_prog",
  "Gran-lin" = "gran", "Monocyte prog" = "mono_prog", "Monocyte-lin" = "mono",
  "Neutrophil-lin" = "neut", "Erythroid-lin I" = "eryth1",
  "Erythroid-lin II" = "eryth2", "MK-lin" = "mk", "Lymphoid prog" = "lym_prog",
  "B-lin" = "bcell", "Total dead cells" = "dead_cells"
)
simCtl |>
  select(time, all_of(cellCols)) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "cell", values_to = "count") |>
  mutate(cell = factor(cell, levels = names(cellCols))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, count)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#C2185B") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 1e7)) +
  facet_wrap(~cell, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Cells/mL",
       caption = "Replicates the model lines of Figure 3 of Wilson 2020 (drug-free kinetics).") +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper does not print the Figure 3 values. The day-6 end points of its
model lines were read by eye from the log-scale panels, to about 0.1
decade, and the packaged model reproduces each one to within 0.3 decade:

```{r fig3-check}
fig3Day6 <- c(
  hsc = 3.7, mpp = 3.85, gmp = 4.5, gran_prog = 3.9, gran = 4.9,
  mono_prog = 4.0, mono = 4.5, neut = 4.7, eryth1 = 4.9, eryth2 = 5.2,
  mk = 4.1, lym_prog = 2.7, bcell = 3.2, dead_cells = 4.9
)
simLog6 <- log10(unlist(simCtl[simCtl$time == 6, names(fig3Day6)]))
data.frame(
  cell = names(fig3Day6),
  figure3_log10 = fig3Day6,
  simulated_log10 = round(simLog6, 2)
) |>
  rename("State" = cell, "Figure 3, log10 cells/mL (by eye)" = figure3_log10,
         "Simulated, log10 cells/mL" = simulated_log10) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(abs(simLog6 - fig3Day6) < 0.3))
```

The shapes also match. Lymphoid progenitors are the only lineage that
declines (the Discussion comments on this), and neutrophils dip over the
first two days before expanding steeply.

## The neutrophil split at t = 0 instead of t = 0.01 day

In SimBiology, the neutrophils start as one proliferating pool of 154.07
cells/mL, and an event at t = 0.01 day moves 99.974% of the *initial* count
into a quiescent pool. The packaged model applies the split at t = 0. The
exact SimBiology behaviour can be reproduced with rxode2 replacement events
(`evid = 5`): start with `qf_neut = 0` (everything proliferating) and replace
both pools at t = 0.01 day.

```{r neut-event}
qf <- ui$theta[["qf_neut"]]
n0 <- ui$theta[["bl_neut"]]
evExact <- et(amt = 0, cmt = "drug", time = 0) |>
  et(time = 0.01, amt = qf * n0, cmt = "neut_quies", evid = 5) |>
  et(time = 0.01, amt = (1 - qf) * n0, cmt = "neut_prolif", evid = 5) |>
  et(c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6))
simExact <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(ui, evExact, params = c(qf_neut = 0)))
simT0 <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(ui, et(amt = 0, cmt = "drug", time = 0) |> et(c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6))))
relDiff <- sapply(c(unname(cellCols), "totalViableCells"), function(k) {
  max(abs(simT0[[k]] / simExact[[k]] - 1))
})
signif(relDiff[relDiff > 0], 2)
# Only the neutrophil pools and the downstream sums can move; everything
# upstream of the neutrophils is untouched by the event.
stopifnot(
  max(relDiff) < 0.03,
  max(relDiff[c("hsc", "mpp", "gmp", "gran", "eryth1", "mk", "bcell")]) < 1e-6
)
```

The SimBiology event discards the 0.01 day of growth of the small
proliferating pool at the moment of the split. As a result, day-6
neutrophils differ by `r signif(100 * relDiff[["neut"]], 2)`%, and total dead
and total viable cells by less than 0.2%. Every cell type upstream of the
neutrophils is identical. The t = 0 split is kept for simplicity. Use the
event table above to reproduce the SimBiology trajectories exactly.

# Drug effects

```{r table1}
tab1Long <- tab1 |>
  pivot_longer(-parameter, names_to = "drug", values_to = "table1") |>
  mutate(

    cell = cellKey[sub("^(EC50_|Emax_T_)", "", parameter)],
    s2 = mapply(function(k, cl, dr) {
      if (k == "EC50") exp(drugPar[[dr]][[paste0("lec50_", cl)]])
      else drugPar[[dr]][[paste0("emaxt_", cl)]]
    }, kind, cell, drug)
  )
stopifnot(!anyNA(tab1Long$cell), nrow(tab1Long) == 26 * 8)
maxRoundErr <- max(abs(round(tab1Long$s2, 3) - tab1Long$table1))
maxRoundErr
stopifnot(maxRoundErr < 1e-9)
```

## Replicates Figure 7 of Wilson 2020

EmaxT * C / (C + EC50) per cell type over the tested concentrations. Values
above 1 (dashed line) mean cell killing on top of a complete block of
proliferation.

```{r fig7, fig.height = 6}
refDrugs <- c("abemaciclib", "dinaciclib", "ribociclib", "palbociclib",
              "paclitaxel", "docetaxel", "thalidomide", "pictilisib")
concs <- c(0.2, 1, 5, 25, 100, 500, 2500)
fig7 <- expand.grid(drug = refDrugs, cell = unname(cellKey), conc = 10^seq(-1, 3.5, by = 0.05),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  mutate(effect = mapply(function(dr, cl, cc) {
    p <- drugPar[[dr]]
    p[[paste0("emaxt_", cl)]] * cc / (cc + exp(p[[paste0("lec50_", cl)]]))
  }, drug, cell, conc))
ggplot(fig7, aes(conc, effect, colour = cell)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Concentration (nM)", y = "EmaxT * C / (C + EC50)", colour = "Cell type",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 7 of Wilson 2020 as line plots instead of heat maps.") +
  theme_bw()
```

As in the paper, docetaxel, paclitaxel and dinaciclib reach effects above 1
(cell killing). All three kill HSC, granulocytes and early erythroid cells.
Docetaxel also kills MPP, both taxanes kill monocyte progenitors, and
dinaciclib kills lymphoid progenitors. By contrast,
palbociclib acts mainly on HSC and GMP and stays below 1
(anti-proliferation only).

```{r dose-response}
obsCols <- c(HSCs = "hsc", MPPs = "mpp", GMPs = "gmp", GranPs = "gran_prog",
             Gran = "gran", MonoPs = "mono_prog", Mon = "mono", Neut = "neut",
             ErythI = "eryth1", ErythII = "eryth2", MK = "mk", LymP = "lym_prog",
             Blin = "bcell", total_live = "totalViableCells",
             total_dead = "dead_cells")
simDay6 <- function(drug, conc) {
  ev <- et(amt = conc, cmt = "drug", time = 0) |> et(6)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(ui, ev, params = drugPar[[drug]]))
  s[s$time == 6, unname(obsCols)]
}
ctl6 <- simDay6("docetaxel", 0)
simResp <- expand.grid(drug = refDrugs, dose = concs, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
simResp <- bind_cols(simResp, do.call(rbind, Map(simDay6, simResp$drug, simResp$dose)))
simResp[unname(obsCols)] <- sweep(as.matrix(simResp[unname(obsCols)]), 2,
                                   as.numeric(ctl6), "/")
names(simResp) <- c("drug", "dose", names(obsCols))
gof <- inner_join(
  pivot_longer(obs, -c(drug, dose), names_to = "cell", values_to = "observed"),
  pivot_longer(simResp, -c(drug, dose), names_to = "cell", values_to = "simulated"),
  by = c("drug", "dose", "cell")
)
stopifnot(nrow(gof) == 8 * 7 * 15)
```

```{r dose-response-plot, fig.height = 9}
ggplot(gof, aes(dose)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = observed), shape = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = simulated, colour = drug)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_grid(cell ~ drug) +
  labs(x = "Concentration (nM)", y = "Day-6 count / vehicle control",
       caption = "Replicates Supplementary Figures S1-S8 of Wilson 2020 (circles: S1 Table; lines: model).") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 7) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Mean squared error per compound, with the paper's lymphoid-progenitor column
shown separately (see Assumptions and deviations):

```{r mse}
mseTab <- gof |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(cell == "LymP", "LymP", "other")) |>
  group_by(drug, group) |>
  summarise(mse = mean((observed - simulated)^2),
            medAbs = median(abs(observed - simulated)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(mse, medAbs))
mseTab |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Compound" = drug,
    "MSE, lymphoid progenitors" = mse_LymP,
    "MSE, other 14 outputs" = mse_other,
    "Median |obs - sim|, lymphoid progenitors" = medAbs_LymP,
    "Median |obs - sim|, other 14 outputs" = medAbs_other
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
# Deterministic simulation of the paper's own fitted parameters against its
# own fitting data: a mis-transcribed flux, stoichiometry or parameter moves
# these errors by far more than the margins below.
stopifnot(
  all(mseTab$medAbs_other < 0.12),
  all(mseTab$mse_other < 0.04)
)
```

Outside the lymphoid progenitors, the model reproduces the assay data with a
median absolute error below 0.1 on the vehicle-normalized scale for every
reference compound, including the thalidomide negative control. The mean
squared errors are largest for docetaxel and paclitaxel, the two compounds
with the strongest cell-killing effects.

## Drug-free sanity check

With every EmaxT at zero, the drug state has no effect at any concentration:

```{r inert}
simHigh <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(ui, et(amt = 2500, cmt = "drug", time = 0) |> et(6)))
simZero <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(ui, et(amt = 0, cmt = "drug", time = 0) |> et(6)))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(simHigh$totalViableCells, simZero$totalViableCells)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(simHigh$dead_cells, simZero$dead_cells)))
```

# NCA

Non-compartmental analysis does not apply. The model has no pharmacokinetics:
the in vitro drug concentration is constant for the whole culture, and every
output is a cell count. The quantitative validation here is the
concentration-response comparison above against the paper's own fitting data
(S1 Table).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Neutrophil split at t = 0.** S1 Text splits the neutrophils into
  quiescent and proliferating pools with an event at t = 0.01 day. The
  packaged model applies the split as an initial condition. The exact event
  is reproduced above with `evid = 5`. Day-6 neutrophils differ by about 2%,
  and no upstream cell type changes.
* **Lymphoid progenitors were not part of the drug-effect fit.** The
  Methods list of cell types fitted in the drug-effect step ("hematopoietic
  stem cells ... and B cells (B-lin)") and the rows of Figure 4 both omit
  lymphoid progenitors, although S2 Table carries an EmaxT and EC50 for
  them. The Methods text says 13 cell types but lists only 12. The assay's lymphoid-progenitor counts fall with concentration for
  most compounds, but the fitted EmaxT for this cell type is near zero for
  all reference compounds except dinaciclib, so the model barely moves. This
  matches the model as published, not a transcription error, and the
  lymphoid-progenitor misfit is reported separately above.
* **`renewal_Mono` is not carried.** S1 Text lists `renewal_Mono = 0.26505`,
  but no flux uses it (monocyte-lineage cells are terminal and proliferate
  without renewal), so it has no effect on the model.
* **Named compounds only.** S2 Table has drug-effect parameters for 51
  compounds, 37 of them anonymized development compounds (`class2_drug1`,
  `Pi3K_drug4`, ...). The 14 named compounds are carried in
  `drugEffectParameters`; 5-FU is keyed as `fluorouracil`. Values come from
  the sheet of fitted natural-log EC50s. The sheet of EC50s is its
  exponential and agrees with Table 1.
* **Drug-free defaults.** `lec50_* = 1` is the SimBiology default and has no
  effect while `emaxt_* = 0`. It is not an estimate.
* **No variability.** The paper fitted donor-mean data by a genetic algorithm
  with local search and reports no between-donor variability or residual
  error, so none is encoded.
* **Units.** SimBiology counts cells as `molecule` in a 1 mL compartment.
  The states are therefore cells/mL, the unit of Figure 3. The drug state is
  a concentration in nM (the unit of EC50), set by a bolus with
  `amt` = concentration.
